question: Which of the following is used as a cooling medium for the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the superconducting magnets in MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Helium:-**

 
 
• It​** **is used as a** cooling medium** for the** Large Hadron Collider** (LHC) and the **superconducting magnets in MRI scanners **and **NMR spectrometers** due to its ability to remain in a** liquid state a**t extremely low temperatures.
 
• Helium is a **noble gas and is non-reactive**, making it an ideal cooling medium for sensitive equipment.
 
• In the LHC, helium is used to **cool the superconducting magnets** to temperatures close to absolute zero (-273.15°C) in order to maintain their superconductivity.
 
• In MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers, helium is used to** cool the superconducting coils** which create the** strong magnetic fields** needed for imaging.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neon:-**

 
 
• It is a** noble gas** and is also **non-reactive like helium**, but it has a** lower boiling point** and is not as** efficient at cooling.**
 
 
 
• **Chlorine:-**
 
 
• It is a **halogen** and is **highly reactive**, making it unsuitable for use as a **cooling medium.**
 
 
 
• **Argon:- **
 
 
• **​**It** **is a **noble gas** like helium and neon, but it has a** higher boiling point** than helium and is not as efficient at cooling.
